html:
The largest country of Central Asia and the ninth largest in the world, independent since December 1991. The map shows it in 1994 and 2010.

Kazakhstan was the last Soviet republic to declare independence, days before the Soviet Union dissolved. It inherited Soviet nuclear weapons, which it gave up, and the Semipalatinsk test site, closed in 1991 after decades of nuclear tests that harmed people living nearby. Russia kept its lease on the Baikonur Cosmodrome.

Nursultan Nazarbayev, the Soviet-era leader, ruled until 2019. He moved the capital from Almaty to Astana in 1997 and filled it with grand new buildings. Caspian oil, and gas sent east through the pipeline to China, made the country the richest in the region, with its own currency, the tenge, from 1993.

Kazakhs became a majority again only after independence, as many Russians and Germans left. The state traces its roots to the Kazakh Khanate of the 15th century, and in 2017 it began moving Kazakh to the Latin script.
